clips.title: Building Effective Agents with LangGraph
clips.why: The evaluator-optimizer pattern from Anthropic's "Building effective agents": one model produces, another grades and gives feedback, and the loop repeats until the grade is good. Our self-review is this pattern.
look: The evaluator returns a structured grade plus feedback, not free text. Our reviewer returns findings with a severity.
The loop's end is a condition (the evaluator is satisfied), not a number of rounds.
Think about what his loop would do if the evaluator kept asking for the same change. That is the gap our fingerprints close.
clips.after: Nova's loop adds two things to the pattern: the evaluator is a fresh session each round, and a finding that returns after a fix goes to a person.

clips.title: Claude Code Now Has Eyes | Playwright MCP Integration
clips.why: A separate agent that looks at the running app through Playwright MCP instead of reading the code: the idea behind our QA agent.
look: The browser agent checks what is on the screen, not what the code says.
It is given a focused job, separate from the agent that wrote the code.
Notice what it reports back. Ours reports pass or fail per QA check, what it saw, and a video.
clips.after: Our QA agent is its own session, not a subagent of Nova, and it may not read the checkout at all, so it can only judge what a user would see.

practice.q: Which reader gets only the ticket and the diff?

options.why: It also gets the approved plan, so it can check every plan item is done.
Ticket and diff, nothing else, so it judges each change only by whether the ticket needs it.
The QA agent gets no diff at all: only the QA plan and the running app.

practice.q: Finish the fingerprint so a finding that moves to a new line keeps the same fingerprint.
practice.hint: The finding's message, after numbers are removed.
practice.why: File, rule and normalised message. Adding f.line would give every moved finding a new fingerprint and bring ping-pong back.

practice.q: A finding was fixed in round 1 and is back in round 2 with the same fingerprint. What does the loop do?

options.text: Fixes it again, more carefully this time
options.why: The same fix argument would repeat. The fingerprint says this already failed once.

options.text: Asks the requester in the ticket's Slack thread and lists the finding as left
options.why: A returning finding means the fix did not hold or the two sides disagree. A person decides.

options.text: Removes the finding, because the reviewer is clearly wrong
options.why: Nobody knows yet who is wrong. Hiding it would also hide it from the PR's reviewers.

practice.q: Put one round of the self-review loop in order.
items: A fresh reviewer session reads the ticket, the plan and the diff
Each important finding gets a fingerprint
Nova fixes each new finding or answers with a reason; a returning one goes to a person
The harness reruns the QA checks
If nothing important is open, the scope judge reads the final diff once
practice.why: Review, fix, recheck, and only when the reviewer is clean does the scope judge look at the final diff.

practice.q: Why does every round rerun the QA checks?

options.text: Because the reviewer cannot read test output
options.why: The reason is about the fixes, not the reviewer.

options.text: Because a fix for a review finding can quietly break a check the requester approved
options.why: Fixes are new code. The approved checks must stay green after every round, not only at the end.

options.text: To produce more videos for the PR
options.why: Videos come from the QA agent's browser run, not from rerunning the tests.
